newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling front to meet on budget Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling front to meet on budget Wednesday.

text.p: Members of India's ruling United Front will meet on Wednesday to seek ways to get the groundbreaking 1997/98 (April-March) budget approved by the parliament, the party spokesman said on Monday.
"The Steering Committee of the United Front is going to meet on April 9 at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT)," United Front spokesman S. Jaipal Reddy told a briefing.
"We will oursevles take a collective view on the budget. After that we will approach the speaker and then get in touch with other parties to evolve a consensus," he added.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence on April 11 following the decision by the Congress party, his former make-or-break ally, to withdraw support to the 10-month old government.
Most political parties have said they would not allow the political crisis to derail the budget presented by Finance Minister P.Chidambaram on February 28.
But they have offered different solutions to end the impasse, including a proposal to take up the discussion on budget after the vote of confidence.
Reddy told reporters the United Front had not abandoned the idea of getting the federal budget passed by the Lok Sabha before the confidence vote.
"The idea is still there. But the idea has to be okayed by the steering committee. Then all other political parties must agree because such a procedure will involve waiver of many rules," Reddy said.

Asked if the budget would be passed before the confidence vote and without a debate Reddy said: "That will depend on the consensus that is evolved by the Speaker in consultation with all the parties."
Industry and trade bodies have urged all political parties to get the budget, which radically lowered income tax and slashed corporate tax and reduced import tariffs, approved in the parliament.
